transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I'm here because I've been feeling persistently depressed and sad for a really long time, about two years and two months now. It just feels like this constant low mood that I can't seem to shake.
Did these feelings start after a specific stressful event or major life change, or did they come on without a clear trigger?
I honestly can't recall a specific event or any clear trigger that started all of this. It feels like these feelings just came on gradually over time, rather than starting from one particular moment.
During these past two years, have there been any stretches of two months or longer when you were not feeling depressed at all?

No, I haven't had any breaks like that. I have been feeling down and depressed continuously for the entire two years and two months. There hasn't been a time where I felt better or symptom-free for even two months.

During this time, have there been periods of at least two weeks when your depression became much worse and you also had several other symptoms like loss of interest, sleep or appetite changes, low energy, poor concentration, guilt, or thoughts of death?

No, I haven't really experienced distinct two-week periods where things suddenly got much worse with thoughts of death or a loss of interest. Instead, my low mood, sleep issues, and feelings of worthlessness have just been relatively constant and continuous over the past two years and two months.
Along with the low mood, have you also had poor appetite or overeating, low energy, low self-esteem, poor concentration, or trouble making decisions during this time?

Yes, I've definitely struggled with my appetite, either barely eating or overeating, and my self-esteem is extremely low because I constantly feel worthless and inferior to everyone else. On the other hand, I haven't really noticed having low energy, poor concentration, or any trouble making decisions.
Have you ever had a period lasting several days when you felt unusually energetic or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or were more impulsive than normal?
No, I've never had any periods like that. I've never felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or needed less sleep. My mood has just been consistently low and depressed this entire time.
How much has this ongoing depression affected your work, school, relationships, or daily functioning?

Honestly, I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought about it in those specific terms. Since I've felt this way for so long, it has just become my normal, so it's hard to say how much it has actually affected my work or relationships.
Can you give me one or two specific examples of how this low mood has affected your daily life, like your work, relationships, or ability to take care of yourself?

It is really hard to point to specific examples since this has just become my everyday reality. Generally, I just feel too exhausted or lack the confidence to handle basic daily tasks, so I tend to pull back from things.
Even if your mood has been low most of the time, have you also lost interest or pleasure in activities you usually enjoy for at least two weeks at a time?

No, I haven't really experienced a complete loss of interest or pleasure in my activities. I might not feel super excited about things, but I wouldn't say I've completely lost interest for weeks at a time.
You mentioned sleep issues—have you mostly had trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much during this time?

I actually struggle with all of those. I often have a really hard time falling asleep and wake up frequently during the night, but there are also periods where I end up sleeping for way too long. No matter how much sleep I get, I never feel rested.
